main_score: Pearson at zero lag on standardized, interpolated, smoothed curves
lag_sign: positive: music change occurs later than video (corr(v(t),m(t+lag)))
lag_support: same video anchors at all lags, trimmed by 2s on both sides; minimum 5s
time_alignment: paired clips assumed to share clip start; use first decoded sample/frame as zero; no fitted shift
grouping: top/bottom ceil(20% of quality-ok clips), descriptive only; ties ordered by clip_id
caveats: No hypothesis-test p-values: samples are autocorrelated
50 clips are a selected subset, not a random sample of OSSL
Smoothing and MusicFM context affect correlation; paired start alignment is an assumption

absolute_difference.definition: Absolute differences use the same saved, independently standardized, 25 Hz aligned and 1.2-second Hann-smoothed curves as the primary Pearson score, at zero lag over the full common interval. For each sample, d(t) = |video(t) - music(t)|; mean absolute difference = mean(d), median absolute difference = median(d). Lower is better (0 means identical curves), in standardized curve units, not raw audio/video units. Pearson is higher-is-better and measures co-variation; absolute difference also reflects amplitude mismatch. Smoothing changes amplitude, so these values should only be compared with the same preprocessing. Ranks and high/low groups remain based on Pearson; neither metric measures perceptual music quality.
